name: Mixe, Totontepec
catalog_quote: placement of the full-stress syllable which is the center of the phonemic-word is not predictable relative to phonemic-word boundaries. ... With the exception of forms in which certain stressed verbal suffixes occur, the full-stressed syllable, in any TM morphemic-word also constituting a phonemic-word, is the root syllable, or in the case of polysyllabic roots, the first syllable of the root.
readall_conflicts: The only listed work (Van Haitsma & Van Haitsma 1976) reports a phrase/clause-level accent on the head word, final if the last syllable is closed or has a non-short/glottalized nucleus, else penultimate — a weight-sensitive final/penult pattern, not the fixed: initial syllable pattern the catalog records for Totontepec Mixe from StressTyp2. This is not a direct conflict because the sketch describes San José El Paraíso Mixe (Coatlán-area, mco), which the authors distinguish from the Totontepec dialect

audit.recode_to: Drop the 'initial at all lengths' dominant rule (100, 1000..). Descriptive rule stays Crawford's: stress is morphological/lexical (root syllable, first syllable of polysyllabic roots; last stressed verbal suffix when present). Dominant surface pattern should be right-edge: penult by default, final when the final nucleus is long/rearticulated (weight-sensitive; set 'heavy'), per Santos Martínez 2013:233-234 and consistent with Crawford 1965:302-303 orthographic defaults; for disyllables this coincides with initial (66%), which is where the current 'initial' coding came from. If the editor prefers not to adopt an MA-thesis rule, minimum fix is classification lexical/morphological with 2-syll initial-dominant only and no extrapolation to 3+ syllables.
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim at Crawford 1963:108-109 sec. 3.111 (PDF p.120-121) in the held scanned/PDF. (2) The deciding source is the primary phonology monograph and is appropriate, but what it states is root-governed (not word-position) stress; the catalog's 'fixed-dominant initial 10/100/1000/..' is an extrapolation. Our own held token census does not support it beyond disyllables (2-syll 8 initial vs 2 final; 3-syll 3 initial vs 3 medial; 4-syll 0 initial, 3 second, 2 third; 49 of 80 tokens monosyllabic). (3) Two independent held/downloaded sources point to a right-edge, weight-sensitive dominant pattern instead: Crawford's own 1965 Notas (accent predictable enough to omit when on the last complex-nucleus syllable, else closed final, else penult: 'la mayoría de las palabras') and Santos Martínez 2013 (same variant, acoustic MA thesis: moraic trochee from the right edge; penult unless fin

sources.quote: p.227: 'de 41 bisílabos, 27 recaen en la sílaba inicial y 14 en la sílaba final' (66% initial). p.233-234 summary: '1. Cuando la sílaba final tiene vocal breve /V/ o vocal breve cortada /Vˀ/ el acento cae en la penúltima sílaba... 2. Cuando la sílaba final tiene vocal larga /Vː/, vocal larga cortada /Vːˀ/ ó vocal rearticulada VˀV el acento se mueve hacia esa misma sílaba. En términos más formales, se forman pies trocaicos-moraicos a partir del extremo final de la palabra.' Tri/tetrasyllabic examples are penult: tə.ˈdəʊh.tək 'ocho', ti.kɨ.ˈla.ja 'lagartija'; three lexical exceptions with final
